name: Artifact-Centric Self-Evolution
title: Artifact-Centric Self-Evolution for Autonomous AI Research Agents
core_hypothesis: Agents improve more reliably when they evolve persistent executable artifacts, rubrics, and strategy policies instead of only rewriting prompts.
related_work_gap: AI Scientist-v2 demonstrates agentic tree search for workshop-level discovery, while self-evolving agents often focus on games or coding tasks; the missing link is controlled self-evolution inside the research lifecycle itself.
expected_novelty: A reproducible protocol for measuring policy/artifact evolution across repeated research cycles.
minimal_experiment: Compare fixed single-agent, prompt-reflection, and artifact-evolution variants on 10 to 20 research-lifecycle tasks.
evaluation_target: Task completion, claim-grounding errors, reproducibility score, reviewer score, and token-normalized performance.
main_risk: LLM judges may overvalue polished writing; include executable checks and blind human spot review.

name: Collaboration Topology Ablation
title: Which Multi-Agent Collaboration Topologies Help Automated Research?
core_hypothesis: Graph/tree-style collaboration with explicit critic and experiment-manager roles will outperform chain or single-agent coordination for research planning and result validation.
related_work_gap: MultiAgentBench evaluates collaboration broadly, but automated scientific research has domain-specific failure modes such as unsupported novelty claims and broken experiments.
expected_novelty: A research-agent-specific topology ablation with controlled budgets and scientific quality metrics.
minimal_experiment: Run single, chain, tree, and graph teams on the same task suite and compare milestone completion plus quality metrics.
evaluation_target: Milestone completion, conflict resolution quality, executable experiment rate, and final paper-review score.
main_risk: More agents consume more tokens; normalize by total tokens and add a same-budget single-agent baseline.

name: VLM Figure Critic Loop
title: Vision-Language Figure Critiques as a Bottleneck in Automated Paper Writing
core_hypothesis: A VLM critic reduces misleading or unreadable figures and improves paper review scores when integrated after plot generation.
related_work_gap: AI Scientist-v2 reports a VLM feedback loop for figures; a focused ablation can quantify when it matters and when it is unnecessary.
expected_novelty: A small, controlled study of figure-feedback value under realistic API cost constraints.
minimal_experiment: Generate result plots with and without VLM critique; score readability, correctness, and paper-level impact.
evaluation_target: Figure defect rate, VLM-human agreement on figure issues, and reviewer score delta.
main_risk: Requires Monica/VLM API integration and figure-heavy tasks; keep as a secondary experiment.

name: Literature-Grounded Novelty Guard
title: Literature-Grounded Novelty Guards for AI-Generated Research Ideas
core_hypothesis: Structured novelty checks against retrieved literature reduce duplicate or overclaimed AI-generated research ideas without suppressing useful incremental work.
related_work_gap: Existing autonomous research systems search literature, but few isolate novelty-check quality as a measured component.
expected_novelty: A benchmarked novelty-guard module with false-positive and false-negative analysis.
minimal_experiment: Create tasks with known related-work traps; compare no retrieval, shallow retrieval, and structured novelty-guard variants.
evaluation_target: Duplicate detection, claim calibration, accepted idea rate, and downstream reviewer novelty score.
main_risk: Requires high-quality literature labels; start with curated small labels.
